sections.en: Total market capitalization stands near $1,699.6B (CoinGecko). Reported 24-hour spot volume is $37.32B with 7-day average turnover broadly normal versus the trailing month (1.00x) . Note: the ETF-flow and sentiment figures above are the public Farside and alternative.me series; proprietary on-chain datasets are still left out rather than estimated. The alternative.me Fear & Greed gauge prints 70 (Greed). Spot-BTC ETF net inflow for 18 Sep 2026 was $433.0m (Farside).

**Derivatives positioning.** The public Binance futures endpoints did not answer for this asset on this cycle, so rather than fabricate a view the desk flags it as a **data gap**: funding and open-interest extremes remain the standard trigger for squeeze dynamics in Bitcoin.

**Trend structure.** Across horizons the picture is perfect bullish alignment (price > EMA20 > EMA50 > EMA200), the textbook configuration of a trend-following regime where pullbacks into the 20-day mean tend to be bought. Spot at $84,573 versus EMA20 $78,583, EMA50 $74,909 and EMA200 $74,389 frames the medium-term bias mechanically rather than emotionally. From this configuration the desk's working assumption is that trend-following exposure is only justified while price holds the side of the 50-day average it currently occupies.

**Key levels.** The operational map reads: initial support at $81,272 (recent swing low); the lower Bollinger band $74,355 as the 2σ downside envelope; upper band $83,272 as the stretch target. Levels derived from the last ~60 sessions of closes are guides for location, not promises of reaction; they mark where prior two-way business was done and therefore where resting liquidity is most plausible. ATR(14) of $2,305 implies a typical daily range of roughly 2.7 percent of spot, which is the unit of risk to size positions against.

**Momentum.** RSI(14) prints 70.9 — overbought territory; MACD (12/26/9) sits above its signal line (1807 vs 1539, histogram +267.7), consistent with building momentum. Momentum readings are state descriptors, not trade signals on their own; the desk treats confluence between momentum and level location as the actionable unit.

**Volatility & liquidity.** 30-day realized volatility annualizes near 39%; the 20-day band spans 11% of the mid — compressed, which often precedes a volatility expansion; 7-day turnover runs at 1.00x the trailing-month norm. Behavior around these regimes — absorption at band edges, volume confirmation on breaks — is what separates a tradeable move from noise.

**Performance context.** On longer windows the asset has returned +9.72% over 30 days and +34.95% over 90 days. Positioning decisions made on monthly horizons should respect these base rates instead of extrapolating the last week. The 7-session change (+8.20%) is the shortest window the desk treats as signal rather than noise.

sections.en:
**Bullish scenario.** Continuation higher requires continued holds of the 50-day average ($74,909); RSI holding above 60 (currently 71). Under those conditions the path of least resistance flips to buy-the-dip, with prior resistance converting to support as the confirmation test.

**Bearish scenario.** Downside continuation triggers on a decisive loss of $81,272. In that case failed support typically becomes the new ceiling, and momentum chasers provide the exit liquidity.

Net take on Bitcoin: spot $84,610 with the medium-term bias constructive while price holds the relevant side of the 50-day average. The 24-hour tape (+5.15%) is consistent with that bias. Decision zones are the levels named in the technical section, not opinions: trade the reaction at those prices, not the headline of the day.
